To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gramicidin channel has an alpha-helix structure and a 3(10)-helix structure in the membrane, that the channel has two conformational substates, that the channel can adopt a third conformational substate in the membrane, and that the conformational sub-states of the channel can be described quantitatively by the free-energy surface.
(1) The gramicidin channel is a solvable protein folding problem, in that the sequence encodes the conformational properties of the channel.

(i) the linear gramicidin channels form a single-file dimer in lipid bilayers; (ii) each monomer in a dimer is a helical structure; (iii) the helices in a dimer are aligned in parallel; (iv) the helices have a right-handed twist; and (v) the helix axis is tilted by 30-35 degrees relative to the membrane normal.
